title: Epidamnos founded
description: Greek colonists from Corinth and Corcyra found Epidamnos, later Dyrrachium, on the Illyrian coast.

title: Apollonia founded
description: Greek colonists found Apollonia, which becomes a leading port and a centre of learning in Roman times.

title: Rome defeats King Gentius
description: A Roman army takes the Illyrian capital Scodra and captures King Gentius, ending the Illyrian kingdom.

title: Battle of Dyrrhachium
description: Pompey breaks Julius Caesar's siege lines and forces him to retreat into Thessaly, a month before Pharsalus.

title: Normans defeat the Byzantines at Dyrrhachium
description: Robert Guiscard's Normans rout the army of Emperor Alexios I and go on to take the city.

title: Principality of Arbanon
description: The archon Progon establishes the first known Albanian state, centred on Krujë.

title: Angevin Kingdom of Albania
description: Charles of Anjou proclaims himself King of Albania after his forces take Durrës.

title: Skanderbeg takes Krujë
description: George Kastrioti Skanderbeg deserts the Ottoman army, seizes Krujë with a forged letter and raises his flag over the castle.

title: League of Lezhë
description: Albanian noble families form a military alliance under Skanderbeg that resists the Ottomans for a quarter of a century.

title: First siege of Krujë
description: Sultan Murad II besieges Krujë for months and withdraws without taking it.

title: Death of Skanderbeg
description: Skanderbeg dies of fever, and the resistance he led weakens over the following decade.

title: Siege of Shkodra
description: Mehmed II besieges Venetian-held Shkodër, and its surrender under the peace of 1479 all but completes the Ottoman conquest of Albania.

title: New Academy of Voskopojë
description: A school of higher learning is founded in the merchant town of Voskopojë, then a large trading town.

title: Pashalik of Scutari
description: Mehmed Bushati makes himself pasha of Shkodër, beginning seven decades of near-independent rule by his family in northern Albania.

title: League of Prizren
description: Albanian leaders meet to oppose the cession of Albanian-inhabited land to neighbouring states, the start of the national movement.

title: Congress of Manastir
description: Albanian intellectuals agree on a Latin-based alphabet for the Albanian language.

title: Declaration of independence
description: An assembly led by Ismail Qemali declares Albania independent of the Ottoman Empire during the First Balkan War.

title: Great powers recognise Albania
description: The conference of ambassadors recognises Albania as a principality, with borders that leave about half of all Albanians outside it.

title: Congress of Lushnjë
description: Delegates reject plans to partition the country, form a new government and move the capital to Tirana.

title: Zog proclaimed king
description: President Ahmet Zogu is proclaimed Zog I, King of the Albanians.

title: Italian invasion
description: Italian troops land at Durrës and other ports, King Zog flees and Albania is joined to the Italian crown.

title: Liberation
description: The last German troops leave Shkodër, leaving the country in the hands of Enver Hoxha's communist partisans.

title: Corfu Channel incident
description: Two British destroyers strike mines in Albanian waters, leading to the first case heard by the International Court of Justice.

title: Break with the Soviet Union
description: The Soviet Union cuts diplomatic relations with Albania, which turns to China as its only ally.

title: Death of Enver Hoxha
description: Enver Hoxha dies after four decades in power and is succeeded by Ramiz Alia.

title: Hoxha's statue pulled down
description: Demonstrators topple the statue of Enver Hoxha in the main square, weeks before the first multi-party elections.

title: Unrest of 1997
description: The collapse of pyramid investment schemes sets off an armed revolt in which the state loses control of much of the country.

title: Albania joins NATO
description: Albania becomes a member of the North Atlantic alliance, together with Croatia.
